_comment: `shared` must hold for every implementation that redacts free text: the
browser SDK and the sidecar. A divergence here means one side leaks what
the other removes, which is the kind of gap nobody notices until it is in
`server_only` covers credentials that appear in server logs and never in
a browser. The browser bundle deliberately does not carry these patterns:
it has a size budget, and a page has no Authorization header to log.
`must_survive` is as important as the rest. A scrubber that eats the
diagnostic content is useless, and the line that explains a swallowed
failure is exactly what triage needs.
`prose` covers the heuristic that masks personal data with no shape to
match. It is checked by the sidecar only: the browser never sees a server
log line, and this heuristic is wrong in both directions by design, so it
is corrected afterwards by learned rules rather than trusted absolutely.

shared.name: ssn is labelled as an ssn, not swallowed by the phone rule

server_only.name: jwt survives templating entirely, so it must be matched here
connection string credentials run before the email rule
client ip from a rails request line

must_survive.name: the line that explains a swallowed failure
must_survive.in: ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid rescued: Email has already been taken
must_survive.out: ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid rescued: Email has already been taken

prose.name: a person and a company, which no pattern can match
prose.in: Approved loan for Alice Smith of Acme Holdings

prose.name: a single capitalised word is the log's own language, not a name
http status text must survive: three capitalised words in a row
class and method names are identifiers, never names
sql keywords shout and are left alone
go panic text survives
prose.in: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
prose.out: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address

prose.name: a name at the end of a line
trailing punctuation does not hide a name
